sections.label: Credit bureaus hold individual credit information
sections.summary: Two credit bureaus hold credit information on more than five million individuals, covering over 98% of credit facilities offered to individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, the two credit bureaus hold the credit information of more than five million individuals, on more than 98% of all credit facilities offered to individuals.

sections.label: Credit Bureau Bill licensing objectives
sections.summary: The Credit Bureau Bill 2016 will enable MAS to license and supervise credit bureaus to fulfil two objectives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Moving forward, the Credit Bureau Bill 2016 will enable MAS to license and supervise credit bureaus to fulfil two objectives.

sections.label: MAS consultation on Credit Bureau Bill
sections.summary: MAS consulted industry and public over 18 months, received 32 submissions, and incorporated feedback into the Bill where appropriate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MAS has also consulted extensively with the industry and the public over the last 18 months on the policy changes and the draft Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We received a total of 32 submissions, have studied the feedback received and incorporated it into the Bill where appropriate.

sections.label: Free credit reports and consumer safeguards
sections.summary: The Bill requires licensed credit bureaus to give consumers free credit reports within 30 days of credit application approval or rejection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill further requires licensed credit bureaus to provide individual consumers with free copies of their credit reports, within 30 days of approval or rejection of any credit application.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This will enhance the ability of consumers to review their credit records and help reduce instances of consumers being denied credit due to inaccurate credit data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: A sound, stable and fair credit reporting system supports prudent and sustainable consumer lending practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Credit Bureau Act will help strengthen the credit reporting industry and align our regulatory regime with international best practices while maintaining adequate safeguards for consumers.

sections.label: MAS oversight of credit information
sections.summary: With the Credit Bureau Bill, MAS will oversee credit bureaus' management of customer credit information to safeguard its confidentiality, security and integrity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Data breaches are becoming more widespread, and hacking techniques are growing in sophistication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, with the introduction of the Credit Bureau Bill, I note that MAS will be able to oversee credit bureaus' management of customer credit information, with the objective of safeguarding confidentiality, security and integrity of the information.

sections.label: Fines and consumer rectification rights
sections.summary: MAS should impose fines where lapses are detected, and the Bill allows consumers to access, review and rectify credit records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Where lapses are detected, MAS should impose fines to keep the bureaus on their toes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I also note that the Bill will allow consumers the right to access, review and rectify credit records.

sections.label: Credit card holders defaulting
sections.summary: In 2015, the Credit Bureau Singapore reported that more than 101,493 credit card holders defaulted on their debt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In 2015, the Credit Bureau Singapore (CBS) reported that more than 101,493 credit card holders defaulted on their debt.

sections.label: Free credit reports promotion
sections.summary: From April this year, the CBS offers free credit reports as a promotion to consumers with a credit facility at its 30-member banks and financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The CBS offers as a promotion, free credit reports to consumers who have a credit facility with its 30-member banks and financial institutions, from April this year.

sections.label: Evaluating loans and legitimate credit bureaus
sections.summary: It advises realistically evaluating how to save to repay loans soon and taking loans from legitimate credit bureaus, with MAS licensing credit bureaus to help consumers identify safe, legal ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: When making the purchase, it is important to realistically evaluate how one is going to save in order to pay off the loans in the near future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Furthermore, please take loans from legitimate credit bureaus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Illegal moneylenders may resort to violence and other extreme means to seek repayments and, as their interest rates are not being policed, they are free to set it above however high they wish it to be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With MAS handling the licensing of credit bureaus, this will hopefully help consumers identify the safe, legal credit bureaus for their financial needs.

sections.label: Entities without approved member status
sections.summary: Licensed moneylenders, hire-purchase companies, pawnbrokers and other vendor credit companies are not deemed approved members under the Bill and would not access LCB customer credit information without written consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this regard, I wish to specifically highlight that licensed moneylenders and other entities in the business of providing consumer credit, such as hire-purchase companies, pawnbrokers and other vendor credit companies, are not deemed as approved members under the Bill and, therefore, would not have access to customer credit information held by the LCBs without the customer's written consent.

sections.label: Separate credit bureau regimes
sections.summary: MinLaw set up the MLCB regime in March this year with all licensed moneylenders as contributing members, but separate regimes for moneylenders and for banks and financial institutions leave no overall visibility of an individual's credit assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, I note that the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) has set up a Money Lenders Credit Bureau (MLCB) regime in March this year, involving all licensed moneylenders as contributing members of MLCB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, MLCB only contains customer credit information in respect of loans taken with licensed moneylenders while the LCB regime only deals with credit information from banks and other financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I am concerned that with the separate credit bureau regimes for moneylenders on one hand, and banks and other financial institutions on the other hand, there would be no overall visibility of the credit assessment of an individual.

sections.label: Assessing remaining household credit
sections.summary: Although bank lending accounts for about 98% of household credit granted by commercial entities, assessing credit worthiness of the remaining 2% and protecting that customer information is no less important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Even though as disclosed by the hon Minister in this House on 18 February 2014, bank lending accounts for about 98% of household credit granted by commercial entities, it does not make the objective of assessing credit worthiness of the remaining 2% and protecting the customer information of the same any less important, especially if you were to consider the number of the people involved.

sections.label: Bill silent on customer recourse
sections.summary: The Bill does not state whether customers have recourse if a correction is refused, or whether investigation findings are available to consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Having regard to the objectives of the Bill to protect customer interest in this area, it is noteworthy that the Bill is silent as to whether: (a) the customers have any recourse if the LCB or the approved member refuses to make a correction; and (b) the investigation findings of the LCB or approved member is available to the consumer and subject to review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In Australia, sections 20(u) and 21(w) of the Australian Privacy Act requires a credit reporting body or credit provider that refuses a credit information correction request to, within a reasonable period, give the individual written notice that the correction has not been made and set out the reasons for not correcting the information and explain how the individual may complain about that decision.

sections.label: Consumer recourse and data disputes
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to confirm consumers cannot access investigation findings and can only seek review by the Personal Data Protection Commissioner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the circumstances, could the Minister please confirm that despite sections 18 and 35 of the Bill requiring the LCBs to investigate correction requests, consumers would not have access to such investigation findings and their only recourse against the LCB's refusal to correct the data is to apply to the Personal Data Protection Commissioner to review under section 28 of the PDPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To conclude, notwithstanding my concerns in the three areas, namely, the regulatory framework vis-à-vis licensed moneylenders, treatment of confidential information at the hands of third parties and dealing with data disputes, I agree that formal supervision of credit bureaus and their members is needed to safeguard consumer credit information.

sections.label: Credit applicants never seen reports
sections.summary: A recent report found nine out of 10 credit applicants have never seen their own credit reports when applying for loans or credit cards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In a recent report, it was worrying that nine out of 10 credit applicants have never seen their own credit reports, even as they apply for new loans or new credit cards.

sections.label: Two credit bureaus, CBS monopoly
sections.summary: Only CBS and DPCB will be licensed, and only CBS currently receives comprehensive lender data, prompting a question on MAS monitoring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Currently, as the Minister mentioned, there are only two credit bureaus, the Credit Bureau Singapore (CBS) and the DP Credit Bureau (DPCB), in Singapore, and it is only these two which will be licensed under the new regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In addition, out of these two credit bureaus, it seems that only CBS currently has access to comprehensive data from lenders, as banks are only required to supply data to CBS and not DPCB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As we seem to have a virtual monopoly and unfair advantage in the industry, has MAS been monitoring what effect this has?

sections.label: Bill licenses and supervises credit bureaus
sections.summary: The Bill gives MAS power to license and supervise credit bureaus collecting customer credit information from banks and financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Thus, I applaud the Bill for recognising that the Government must do all it can to ensure that the good is delivered with public interest as a priority.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe this Bill, which provides MAS the power to license and supervise credit bureaus that collect customer credit information from banks and other financial institutions, will promote and ensure sustenance of standards for accuracy, fairness and confidentiality of customer information.

sections.label: FTC study on inaccurate reports
sections.summary: A 2015 Federal Trade Commission study found 23% of customers identified inaccurate information in their credit reports.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2015 study released by the Federal Trade Commission found that 23% of customers identified inaccurate information in their credit reports.

sections.label: Updating credit records process
sections.summary: The speaker supports MAS prescribing the process and turnaround time for updating credit records, preferring consolidated loans and credits for a better overview.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   I support MAS' decision to prescribe the process and turnaround time for updating credit records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although we have the Moneylenders Credit Bureau (MLCB) to which all licensed moneylenders provide information about their loans, it would be better for all loans and credits to be consolidated for a better overview of a client's financial situation.

sections.label: Two-factor authentication access control
sections.summary: An additional layer of access control through two-factor authentication will be required.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: One example is that we will require them to use an additional layer of access control through a two-factor authentication.

sections.label: Reducing unsecured loan quantum
sections.summary: The quantum of unsecured loan will be progressively reduced to 18 months and 12 months in 2017 and 2018 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We agree with Mr Saktiandi that we should tighten such practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Hence, the quantum of unsecured loan will be progressively reduced to 18 months and 12 months in 2017 and 2018 respectively.

sections.label: Consumer credit bureaus data coverage
sections.summary: The two existing consumer credit bureaus already capture information of more than 98% of all credit facilities offered to consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In terms of data comprehensiveness, the two existing consumer credit bureaus already capture information of more than 98% of all credit facilities offered to consumers.

sections.label: Records over last five years
sections.summary: Over the last five years, it is at less than 0.1% of total records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Over the last five years, it is at less than 0.1% of total records.

sections.label: MAS approval for credit report forms
sections.summary: The Bill requires LCBs to seek MAS' approval before making changes to the credit report forms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Bill requires LCBs to seek MAS' approval before making changes to the credit report forms.

sections.label: Free credit reports and fees
sections.summary: The Bill requires LCBs to give a free credit report within 30 days of a credit facility decision, with reports outside that period costing $6.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On the issue of free credit reports, MAS also needs to strike a balance between protecting consumers and keeping operating costs manageable and the service viable and to prevent phishing expeditions and frivolous requests for data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, to protect consumers' interest, the Bill will require LCBs to provide a free copy of a consumer's credit report within 30 days from the date of approval or rejection of a credit facility at the consumer's request.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The approach also minimises the risk of repeated frivolous requests by consumers for their credit reports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But if a consumer wishes to have a credit report outside of this free 30-day period, he can purchase them any time, at $6 a copy, which is not a huge cost barrier.

sections.label: MoneySENSE financial information
sections.summary: Singaporeans are encouraged to use MoneySENSE information to manage finances proactively and use credit responsibly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: To better understand how we can manage our finances proactively and use credit responsibly, I encourage Singaporeans to tap on the wealth of information provided by MoneySENSE − a bit of advertisement here.
